slice: Canonical grouping keys and semantic grouping bit order
status: accepted optional two-file Rust resolver patch; default vendor unchanged

implementation.rule: Strip complete-key aliases, expand repeated ROLLUP/CUBE keys with existing native utilities, canonicalize set membership while retaining occurrences, and prefer a complete set to preserve native key order. Otherwise map native grouping bits to semantic order for SELECT, HAVING and ORDER BY. Store the permutation only on the private grouping ID field.
implementation.reuse: Native grouping operators and unsigned AND/shift/OR expressions; no new kernel, execution node, dependency or Python runtime path.

correctness.new_equivalent_scope: 18 observations in the new 236-observation corpus plus four in the earlier alias-sort corpus. Do not add all 22 to the new strict agreement count.

attempt_00.reason: The physical plan showed two mask/shift terms repeated in projection and sort for common mixed ROLLUP. Prefer a complete set during field discovery to avoid those runtime operations. Preserve the permutation fallback for mixed sets without a complete set.

iterations.final: One complete-set swap is added. All SQL and the full fixed performance schedules remain unchanged.

standard.purpose: Measure grouping-key canonicalization and ordinary grouping/projection controls using the same fixed 160-process schedule.
standard.inference: Use process medians, paired quartet log ratios and fixed seed 172 / 10000 bootstrap resamples. Retain all controls and observations.
standard.runtime: 34efcb6 accepted runtime plus canonical grouping keys and native-bit permutation; identical extended benchmark harness in both binaries
standard.input_limit: 512 integer keys and a nonduplicate grand total produce 513 sorted IDs. Duplicate and full-width correctness is covered separately in the SQL corpus.

mixed.purpose: Complete mixed grouping query versus equivalent explicit GROUPING SETS in the same candidate binary; this includes key-order effects, not an isolated instruction-kernel estimate.

performance_findings.standard: 160 fixed processes. Integer ROLLUP planning instructions +0.066%, execution +0.001%; latency -0.267% and -0.283%. Ordinary grouping and projection instructions remain nearly unchanged. Small time differences also occur in same-binary controls; no universal speedup or zero-cost claim.
performance_findings.mixed: 64 fixed processes comparing mixed ROLLUP with an equivalent explicit GROUPING SETS query in one candidate binary. Planning -4.745% latency and -7.902% instructions. Execution +0.168% latency and +0.003% instructions; same-reference execution control +0.241%. This includes query-shape and set-order effects. It does not isolate bit-permutation cost.
performance_findings.coverage: All 224 processes retained, full perf counter coverage, zero CPU migrations, unchanged ASLR and governor. No concurrent compilation or unrelated investigation during measurement.

final_restoration.note: Final independent hash audit handles absent source files with no sha256 key. The first preflight audit stopped on such a record with KeyError before performance, without modifying any file; build-finally restoration had already passed.

limitations: Agreement includes matching error stages, including two nested-alias parser errors; it is not a supported-query count.
Native semantic plus duplicate ordinal width remains limited to 64 bits.
Three pre-existing computed-addition type differences remain, although grouping rows are repaired.
Original Spark errors and empty-input results remain in the archive; equivalent queries and correct SQL grand totals are checked separately.
The partial-set permutation fallback has correctness coverage but no isolated performance measurement.
Earlier public-ID masking, floating grouping/comparison normalization, dynamic ANSI float-to-integer conversion and USING costs are not eliminated by this slice.
